stage: Additional mechanism robustness study specified after the original factorial outcomes were known and before these new grid and time outcomes. Not an independent confirmatory prediction or external preregistration.
question: Over which input-cost and evaluation-time ranges do the prespecified regulatory programs change their resource ranking, and is the cost-0.2 example sensitive to small changes in the existing counter-path coefficients?
equations: Unchanged seven-state model.derivative; no new state, feedback pathway, coefficient formula or empirical data.
input_subsets: All eight subsets, empty through all three inputs. Selected inputs change only over [5,10); unselected inputs retain their original baseline values.

parameter_neighborhood.scope: Six one-at-a-time coefficient variants, each retaining all eight input programs. Not simultaneous or global parameter sensitivity.

initialization: For each cost or one-at-a-time variant, use the original Experiment.initialize bounded-time relaxation from the same declared upper seed and its original 1e-11 residual criterion. Do not rebalance coefficients and do not select a more favorable stationary branch. Report the seed, converged state, residual, and local eigenvalues. Failure of initialization stops that regime with explicit failure; do not replace it with another seed.
comparators: All program contrasts are within a coefficient regime at the same initial state and elevated opposed-demand schedule. Cross-cost regimes have different equilibrated starting states; differences across costs are not pure direct-cost causal effects. No new pulse-context contrast is required for this within-pulse ranking question; the original context controls remain in the prior record.

integration.method: scipy.solve_ivp DOP853 on the unchanged reference derivative
integration.event_alignment: Separate fixed-forcing integrations over [0,5], [5,10], [10,60], with exact continuous endpoint handoff; no solver stage crosses a forcing discontinuity.
integration.reference_rk4_scope: Cost-0.2 D+R and D+B+R to time60, compared at every common half-unit observation; every cost-0.2 program is also compared with the immutable original fine-grid results at times10 and20.

ranking.rule: Sort resource descending and load ascending; values separated by <= tolerance form a reported tie group. Never impose an ordering within the numerical tie band.
ranking.prespecified_contrast: Resource(D+R)-Resource(D+B+R), retaining all other program rankings rather than selecting only this pair.
ranking.crossings: For each regime, bracket strict sign changes of that contrast on the entire half-unit time grid, refine each bracket using DOP853 dense output with scipy.brentq xtol=1e-8, and report brackets, residuals and two-tolerance agreement. Exact or numerical ties are explicitly retained. A finite horizon does not establish a terminal ordering or an optimum over untested input intensities.

outcomes: All 120 program trajectories at all 101 half-unit post-pulse observation times
All within-regime resource and load rankings, ties and contrasts
All pairwise D+R versus all-three time crossings
Initial-state local stability for all15 regimes
interpretation: A conditional map of this mechanism, synthetic coefficients, finite time window, finite cost grid and six one-at-a-time changes. It does not estimate human effects, calibrate time in days, identify an optimal intervention, prove all seven states necessary, or replace the original outcomes.
output_policy: Write only new regulation-robustness-prefixed files into the existing simulation/regulation-research-results directory. The previous regulation summary, trajectories, protocol, model and package remain unchanged. Refuse absent output directories.
